scope: Coverage-guided fuzzing must exercise parsers, storage log replay, userspace image metadata, sync frames, capability messages, and kernel/user ABI decoding before release.
current_evidence: Adversarial spec tests reject malformed manifests, corrupted storage logs, stale metadata, and bypass attempts.

The release-security checker runs deterministic mutation fuzzing from checked seed corpora against binary cursors, userspace descriptors, ELF image metadata, storage volume loading, sync record decoding, capability messages, and syscall ABI range validation.
graduation_criteria: Keep release-running fuzz harnesses, checked seed corpora, deterministic mutation counts, crash redaction fixtures, and regression tests wired into release-security-check before tagging.
cisa_alignment: Treat exploit-prone input handling as a manufacturer-owned defect class and block release when parser fuzz evidence is absent.

scope: Fault injection must cover boot artifact tamper, rollback failure, service startup, permission review, power loss, torn writes, storage driver crash/rebind, recovery repair, and sync transport disruption.
current_evidence: QEMU smoke paths include service startup, permission review, tampered artifacts, rollback-slot failure, recovery proof, storage durability, sync two-node, and driver restart gates.

The public release-security-gate target aggregates native smoke tamper profiles, storage durability, driver restart, recovery, sync two-node, UEFI QEMU preflight, and the real NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof checker into the release matrix.
graduation_criteria: Keep service startup, permission review, storage, driver, recovery, sync, boot tamper, rollback, UEFI fault campaigns, and the NUC11TNKi5 real-hardware proof bundle in the release matrix with deterministic artifacts and failure triage records.
cisa_alignment: Exercise secure-by-default behavior under failure instead of depending on customer recovery workarounds.

scope: Release artifacts must be buildable from pinned inputs with deterministic outputs or documented, bounded nondeterminism.
current_evidence: The repository pins the Zig toolchain entrypoint and keeps generated artifacts under build outputs.

The reproducible-build-check target copies tracked source into two isolated workspaces, builds release artifacts independently, compares kernel, ISO, signing tool, and userspace image digests, and records the result under build/release-security.
graduation_criteria: Keep a reproducible-build release target that performs two isolated builds, compares artifact digests, records toolchain and environment metadata, and fails on undocumented nondeterminism.
cisa_alignment: Support supply-chain transparency and reduce unverified build inputs before customer distribution.

scope: Every release artifact must carry machine-readable SBOM data, source provenance, signer identity, measured boot inputs, customer-verifiable digest records, and DSSE-wrapped attestations signed by hardware-backed release keys.
current_evidence: Userspace archives, boot measurements, signed bundle state, and launch provenance are modeled and tested.

The release-sbom-provenance target emits artifact-digests.sha256, artifact-measurements.json, SPDX 2.3 SBOM JSON, in-toto/SLSA provenance statements, DSSE provenance envelopes, release keyring metadata, revocation metadata, customer verification policy, and a disclosure dry-run bundle under build/release-security.

The release generator can delegate every DSSE PAE signing operation to a TPM, secure enclave, HSM, or KMS command through ZIGOS_RELEASE_DSSE_SIGN_COMMAND, keeping release code on key handles instead of seed material.

The zigos-verify-release customer CLI validates downloaded artifact digests, DSSE signatures before payload parsing, revoked key ids/generations, SLSA subject digests, artifact measurements, reproducible-build digest evidence, SPDX version metadata, post-quantum keyring policy, and required-mode ML-DSA signature coverage.

The release-security checker rejects release artifact metadata or keyrings that omit DSSE envelopes, hardware-backed key custody, rotation, revocation, customer verifier protocols, artifact measurements, executable verifier tooling, FIPS 203 ML-KEM/FIPS 204 ML-DSA/FIPS 205 SLH-DSA policy, measured rollout, or the explicit statement that ed25519+ml-dsa65 is preview-only and not production FIPS 204 ML-DSA.
graduation_criteria: Generate SPDX SBOMs plus DSSE-wrapped in-toto/SLSA provenance attestations for kernels, userspace images, tools, policy manifests, and ISO outputs.

Sign each DSSE PAE payload with a hardware-backed TPM, secure enclave, HSM, or KMS release key, publish customer-verifiable keyring and revocation metadata, and fail release if the signing key is missing, stale, or revoked.

Keep zigos-verify-release validating artifact digests, DSSE signatures, SLSA subject digests, key generation, revocation status, artifact measurements, reproducible-build evidence, post-quantum policy, and required ML-DSA coverage for every public release.
cisa_alignment: Maintain SBOMs and transparent vulnerability/exploitability records for first- and third-party software.

scope: Threat-model tests must cover explicit authority, privilege boundaries, boot trust, recovery, policy mediation, storage integrity, sync trust, diagnostics privacy, and driver isolation.
current_evidence: Spec conformance and adversarial tests already encode revoked capability, expired lease, malformed manifest, corrupted log, rollback, and bypass threats.

spec/release_security/threat_model.json publishes a reviewer-facing matrix with threat IDs, abuse cases, mitigations, negative tests, residual-risk owners, and release decisions for every required security domain.
graduation_criteria: Keep the threat-model matrix release-gated and require every P0/P1 release track to list abuse cases, mitigations, negative tests, and residual-risk decisions.
cisa_alignment: Make security properties measurable across the product lifecycle and prevent dangerous defaults from shipping silently.

scope: Unsafe Zig and kernel-adjacent sections must be inventoried, reviewed, minimized, and bound by tests before release, especially pointer casts, integer-pointer conversion, inline assembly, packed ABI structs, and user memory copies.
current_evidence: The kernel and native syscall paths centralize many low-level boundaries and have targeted negative tests around user memory and brokered devices.

spec/release_security/memory_safety_inventory.json inventories every tracked Zig source file containing pointer conversion, pointer casts, inline assembly, packed or extern ABI structs, volatile access, or atomic primitives, and the release-security checker rejects any new unsafe source path without release-reviewed owner, mitigation, and test coverage.
graduation_criteria: Keep an unsafe-surface inventory, required audit owner, reviewer checklist, and tests for every user-memory copy, pointer conversion, inline assembly block, and kernel allocator invariant.
cisa_alignment: Treat memory-safety roadmaps and migration/mitigation evidence as mandatory for unsafe or kernel-adjacent code.

scope: Crash dumps, event-ledger exports, remote diagnostics, and support bundles must redact secrets, private object names, personal content, capability tokens, and raw memory by default.
current_evidence: Event-ledger, supervisor, and spec tests verify redacted diagnostics for crashes, permission decisions, and remote shares.

Crash record summaries now redact sensitive reason text by default, and spec/release_security/crash_dump_redaction.json gates raw memory denial, opt-in scoped diagnostics, support-bundle review, and reproducible redaction fixtures.
graduation_criteria: Keep explicit crash dump policy tests for raw memory capture denial, opt-in scoped diagnostics, capability token scrubbing, private object-name scrubbing, and reproducible redaction fixtures.
cisa_alignment: Keep security-sensitive telemetry safe by default and avoid shifting diagnostic privacy risk to customers.

scope: A release must have a published vulnerability disclosure policy, private intake channel, triage SLA, CVE/CWE handling process, coordinated disclosure rules, and security update commitments.
current_evidence: SECURITY.md publishes GitHub private vulnerability reporting and a backup security mailbox, with monitored release-security-review ownership, 3-business-day acknowledgement, 10-business-day triage, coordinated disclosure, CVE/CWE handling, and security update commitments.
spec/release_security/vulnerability_disclosure.json encodes the private intake channels, owner, SLA, CVE/CWE process, and dry-run workflow artifact required by the release gate.
graduation_criteria: Keep the private intake channel published, maintainers on rotation, CVE issuance ownership documented, and end-to-end disclosure dry-run recorded before release.
cisa_alignment: Avoid the CISA bad practice of shipping without a scoped vulnerability disclosure policy and timely CVE/CWE process.

first_hardware_target.selection_reason: Single commodity x86_64 UEFI target with ACPI, integrated display output, USB xHCI input path, M.2 NVMe storage, and wired Intel I225-LM Ethernet so the first hardware proof does not depend on Wi-Fi or dongles.
first_hardware_target.boot_medium: UEFI GRUB ISO or USB image built from build/os.iso.
first_hardware_target.serial_capture: Real-machine serial, framebuffer capture, or HDMI capture logs archived under build/hardware-proofs/nuc11tnki5/ as a complete proof bundle and checked by scripts/check-nuc11tnki5-hardware-proof.sh.
proof_bundle_requirements: proof-manifest.txt must tie the bundle to intel-nuc11tnki5, NUC11TNKi5, real_hardware, serial.log, the sidecar files, the marker contract, the repo commit, capture time, and operator.

serial.log must come from the Intel NUC11TNKi5 and include real-hardware source metadata, exact board SKU metadata, proof-manifest metadata, every required subsystem PASS marker, every booted production-evidence marker, and all minimum cycle counters.
firmware-settings.txt must record BIOS/UEFI version, boot mode, Secure Boot state, storage mode, wake/suspend settings, and any changed firmware options.

power-cycle-notes.txt must record the ten cold boots, ten warm reboots, one hundred NVMe read/write cycles, one hundred I225-LM frame cycles, twenty suspend/resume cycles, ten induced crash-recovery cycles, ten crash-record persistence checks, and ten update rollback power cycles.

artifact-digests.sha256 must record SHA-256 digests for the exact ISO or USB image, kernel, required userspace service images, production readiness manifest, release artifact manifest, hardware marker contract, policy, and driver-set artifacts.
scripts/check-nuc11tnki5-hardware-proof.sh must pass against the proof bundle directory, not a QEMU or OVMF preflight log.
hardware_exit_criteria: Ten cold UEFI boots and ten warm reboots reach native-ready on the NUC11TNKi5 without panic, hang, or firmware fallback.
ACPI table discovery, APIC timer calibration, GOP framebuffer output, USB xHCI keyboard input, NVMe read/write, and Intel I225-LM transmit/receive each emit the required hardware target marker.

Generated userspace startup, service IPC connectivity, compositor framebuffer presentation, permission review rendering, sync replication/restart, driver restart/rebind, crash-record persistence, and update rollback health checks emit the required booted production-evidence markers.
Twenty suspend/resume cycles preserve timer, framebuffer, USB input, NVMe, and network usability.

Ten induced crash-recovery cycles preserve the native store and produce redacted recovery diagnostics, and ten crash-record persistence checks prove those diagnostics survive reboot without exposing raw memory.
Ten update rollback cycles survive real power transitions and return to the verified active slot without losing persisted state.
Every hardware proof bundle includes a proof manifest, serial output, firmware settings, power-cycle notes, and the exact kernel/userspace artifact digests.
open_gaps: No NUC11TNKi5 serial log has been captured from real hardware yet.

The kernel now preserves the GRUB Multiboot handoff, requests a 32-bit framebuffer, validates memory-map and GOP framebuffer descriptors, scans SMBIOS for the NUC11TNKi5 SKU, and composes early ACPI/MADT/FADT/APIC evidence, but those paths have not been captured from the selected NUC firmware.

xHCI keyboard input reports, NVMe read/write cycles, Intel I225-LM transmit/receive cycles, compositor framebuffer presentation, suspend/resume loops, induced crash-recovery loops, persisted crash-record checks, update rollback power-cycle loops, and booted production-evidence markers still need real-device execution and capture.

tracks.title: Object store and storage volume durability
current_evidence: Content-addressed objects use signed metadata, chunked blob records, and Merkle-addressed payload manifests.
The storage volume can save and replay segmented logs through image-backed and attached-volume paths.

Host tests cover corrupted payload rejection, malformed root-log metadata, torn-record rejection, compaction, page-sized payload reload, legacy demo-image migration into the larger envelope, power-loss before root commit, partial-sector log corruption fallback, long-running replay/compaction gates, and shared-memory transfer into the storage service.
The first supported storage envelope is exported from storage_volume.first_supported_capacity_envelope and checked before image or attached-volume persistence.

Writes that exceed the first supported envelope have an explicit user-facing quota policy: reject without partial persistence, report storage.quota.* limit codes, surface NoSpaceLeft at the persistence gate, and load legacy demo-sized images only as migration inputs.

The storage durability QEMU target reuses one native store image across forced reboots, interrupted writes, and one bad root slot, while benchmark thresholds now gate segmented replay and forced checkpoint compaction.
capacity_envelope: Volume image: 786432 bytes across 1536 required device sectors, with 785408 bytes available for replay logs.
Object store: 192 objects, 768 versions, 640 blobs, 224 chunks, 28 chunks per payload, 4096-byte chunks, and a 114688-byte maximum object payload.
Workspace state: 8 workspaces, 96 entries per workspace, and 16 snapshots.
Replay gate: 512 log records and 64 segment boundaries before compaction must write a new checkpoint.
Over-limit write behavior: no truncation, eviction, implicit expansion, or partial persistence; callers must free space or move to a larger product envelope before retrying.
graduation_criteria: Keep the explicit product storage limits enforced in persistence gates or replace fixed tables with bounded dynamic allocation and quota enforcement.
Keep disk-chaos QEMU tests that write, reboot, interrupt, corrupt one slot, compact, and prove deterministic recovery.
Keep benchmark thresholds for storage replay, checkpoint compaction, workspace commit, file-bridge read, and memory pressure at target data sizes.
next_actions: Continue raising the bounded envelope only with matching quota, replay, migration, corruption, QEMU durability, and benchmark evidence.

tracks.title: Boot, attestation, and base update trust chain
current_evidence: Freestanding boot records can be verified against signed artifact manifests and compared across native smoke boots.
Remote attestation refuses emulator-rooted measured state and requires a provisioned non-software root.
A/B base selection, rollback, and post-activation health markers are covered by host logic, QEMU smoke evidence before native-ready, and required real-hardware proof markers.

The native smoke target now includes negative QEMU runs that reject a tampered boot artifact manifest, direct kernel/userspace-image/policy/driver-set measurement tampering, and a rollback target whose slot measurement no longer verifies before the boot can reach native-ready.

The signature envelope and signing CLI now support Ed25519, an Ed25519+ML-DSA-65 hybrid preview profile, and a provider-backed production ML-DSA-65 FIPS 204 profile with full-size signature storage and fail-closed verification for unsupported formats.

A signature-provider boundary and registry now report provider profile, key custody, hardware-backed release eligibility, lifecycle controls, customer-verifier protocol, FIPS 204/FIPS 140 validation metadata, and fail-closed profile mismatches so production Ed25519 or validated ML-DSA providers can be swapped in without changing manifest storage layouts.
Attestation statements carry verifier-visible hardware root key ids and generations, and verifier expectations can reject stale or revoked generations after provider rotation.

Userspace package signatures, boot artifact manifest signatures, generated archive signatures, and attestation statement signatures now route through the default provider registry instead of directly selecting raw Ed25519 operations.

Demo seed packages, SDK simulator release bundles, rendered-shell journeys, package-service fixtures, and spec release fixtures now select the Ed25519 provider explicitly where they model release signing behavior.
production_gaps: Host evidence still uses emulator-provided measurement fallbacks, and attestation root material is represented by software signer identities.
The provider, rotation, revocation, and verifier protocol boundaries exist in source, but the first operational TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS-backed root has not been provisioned on real hardware.

The Ed25519+ML-DSA-65 hybrid profile is a bounded preview commitment for envelope and policy plumbing, not a FIPS 204 ML-DSA implementation; the production path is the separate ml-dsa-65 provider profile with FIPS validation metadata.

Release artifact signing, bootloader measurement handoff, and update rollback now have smoke-level tamper rejection and QEMU rollback markers, but are not yet tied to an operational key-management story or captured on real hardware.
graduation_criteria: Introduce a hardware-root abstraction that supports TPM and secure enclave backed quote/sign operations without exposing root seed material.
Add verifier-facing attestation request and response records with nonce, remote party, policy visibility, key rotation, and revocation tests.

Link an audited FIPS 204 ML-DSA provider through the external provider boundary, publish its validation certificate in the keyring, and move rollout from shadow to canary to required after verifier evidence passes.
Broaden release-image tamper gates from smoke fixtures to direct bootloader measurement mutation cases under operational signing keys.
next_actions: Wire the production root provider interface to the first supported TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS implementation and keep fake providers test-only.
Add hardware proof evidence for root key rotation, revocation propagation, and verifier rejection of stale attestations.

Move explicit software-provider release fixtures onto operational Ed25519 plus ML-DSA key provisioning once the hardware-backed root, FIPS validation metadata, and release key-management interfaces exist.
Add a direct bootloader-measurement mutation fixture and bind the smoke signing path to the production root-provider abstraction.
Capture the update rollback marker group in the NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof bundle.

tracks.title: First real hardware target: Intel NUC11TNKi5
current_evidence: The first supported hardware target is pinned to Intel NUC 11 Pro Kit NUC11TNKi5 instead of a generic PC-compatible bucket.

The target contract enumerates UEFI boot, ACPI tables, APIC timer, GOP framebuffer, USB xHCI input, NVMe block I/O, Intel I225-LM network, compositor framebuffer presentation, suspend/resume, crash recovery, crash-record persistence, and update rollback power cycling as required hardware proof.
The build exposes an OVMF-backed uefi-qemu-test preflight for the ISO path before attempting the same image on the NUC firmware.

The Multiboot entry path now preserves bootloader magic and info pointers, asks GRUB to keep a 32-bit framebuffer payload, and exposes tested memory-map and framebuffer handoff parsers for runtime proof capture.
The kernel tree now has a tested SMBIOS scanner/parser that can match the NUC11TNKi5 SKU from real firmware tables before emitting real-hardware source or board markers.
The kernel tree now has a tested ACPI RSDP parser and aligned scanner as the first non-invasive ACPI building block for the target.
The ACPI parser now validates SDT headers and XSDT/RSDT root-table entries so the hardware proof path can require MADT and FADT presence instead of a standalone RSDP checksum.
The kernel tree now has a tested MADT parser that summarizes local APIC, I/O APIC, interrupt-source override, x2APIC, and PC-AT compatibility data before APIC timer bring-up.
The kernel tree now has a tested FADT parser for PM control blocks, SCI interrupt, PM timer, and reset register plumbing needed before suspend/resume work.
The kernel tree now has a tested UEFI GOP-style linear framebuffer descriptor validator with stride, buffer-size, pixel-format, and text-grid checks.
The kernel tree now has a bounded crash-record format with checksum validation and redacted summary output for later persistent crash recovery.
PCI inventory helpers now identify NVMe controllers and the Intel I225-LM network controller required by the NUC target.
The kernel tree now has a tested NVMe inventory shim with controller-capability parsing, admin-queue validation, and fail-closed data-plane transfer behavior.
The kernel tree now has a tested Intel I225-LM inventory shim with RX/TX ring-plan validation and fail-closed kernel transmit behavior.
The kernel tree now has a tested xHCI input inventory shim with controller-capability parsing, command/event ring validation, and fail-closed USB input report behavior.

A composed kernel hardware-proof module now gates NUC markers on real SKU evidence, Multiboot memory-map and GOP framebuffer handoff, ACPI MADT/FADT discovery, APIC timer readiness evidence, xHCI input evidence, NVMe and I225 cycle counts, suspend/resume counts, redacted crash-recovery counts, crash-record persistence counts, and update rollback power-cycle counts.

The NUC11TNKi5 proof bundle contract now requires real-hardware source metadata, sidecar firmware settings, power-cycle notes, artifact digests, all subsystem PASS markers, all booted production-evidence markers, and minimum cold-boot, reboot, storage, network, suspend/resume, crash-recovery, crash-record persistence, and update rollback counters.

Production readiness rejects QEMU-only evidence for this target; hardware proof requires captured real-machine logs, firmware settings, power-cycle notes, booted service/sync/driver/compositor/permission/update markers, and repeated cold boot, reboot, suspend/resume, storage, network, crash-recovery, crash-record persistence, and update rollback cycles.
production_gaps: The repo can now emit early NUC11TNKi5 proof markers only when the corresponding firmware/handoff facts are present, but no real NUC11TNKi5 boot log has been captured.
UEFI handoff still depends on the GRUB ISO path and has not been proven on the selected NUC firmware.
ACPI RSDP, XSDT/RSDT, MADT, and FADT discovery are wired into early boot proof capture, but APIC timer programming remains proof-readiness evidence rather than interrupt-driven timer replacement.
The framebuffer descriptor validator is wired to Multiboot/GOP-style framebuffer handoff, but real GOP ownership and rendering still need capture on HDMI/framebuffer output.
Crash record formatting is tested but not persisted before reboot or consumed by recovery boot.
PCI target identification, NVMe controller queue validation, and Intel I225-LM ring planning are tested, but NVMe read/write and Intel I225-LM packet I/O drivers are not implemented.
xHCI capability parsing and ring validation are tested, but USB HID keyboard enumeration and input reports are not implemented.

Suspend/resume, crash recovery, crash-record persistence, update rollback across power cycles, compositor framebuffer capture, and booted production-evidence marker capture need real-device implementations and logs.
graduation_criteria: Boot the NUC11TNKi5 from a UEFI USB image built from the repo and archive the serial/framebuffer proof bundle.
Emit and verify every marker in spec/hardware/nuc11tnki5-required-markers.txt from real hardware.
Pass the minimum cycle counts encoded by hardware_target.first_supported_target without panic, hang, unredacted crash data, update rollback loss, or persistence loss.
Keep QEMU smoke, storage durability, driver restart, sync two-node, recovery, and spec gates green before accepting hardware proof as production evidence.
next_actions: Make build/os.iso boot reliably through the NUC11TNKi5 UEFI firmware and record firmware settings.
Capture the new Multiboot memory-map, SMBIOS SKU, ACPI table, APIC timer-readiness, and GOP framebuffer proof markers from the NUC11TNKi5 firmware.
Use scripts/prepare-nuc11tnki5-hardware-proof.sh --build to create the proof manifest, sidecar templates, and artifact digest manifest before capture.
Add xHCI keyboard, NVMe read/write, and Intel I225-LM packet I/O implementations that record real cycle counters before emitting PASS markers.
Add suspend/resume, induced crash-recovery, crash-record persistence, and update rollback power-cycle loops to the NUC proof runbook.
Capture service startup, compositor framebuffer, permission review, sync, driver restart, crash persistence, and update rollback markers in the NUC proof run.

tracks.title: Userspace launch and service image provenance
current_evidence: The build generates a userspace image archive and production artifact manifest for freestanding boot profiles.
Launch provenance, component ABI metadata, signed bundle state, and syscall-dispatched task creation are enforced in native modules.
Negative tests reject unsigned userspace launches and modeled runtime bypasses.
The production-readiness gate rejects unmarked syntheticUserspaceImage fixtures in critical launch and service test paths; existing synthetic fixtures are marked model-only.

The QEMU native smoke gate now requires generated userspace artifacts, scheduler binding, userspace exec/resume probes, service contract registration, service IPC connectivity, and driver restart markers before native-ready.
production_gaps: Many host tests still rely on syntheticUserspaceImage records instead of built image descriptors.
The production archive path needs negative tests for missing image bytes, mismatched digest, bad ELF metadata, and stale generated manifests.
Real-hardware proof still needs to capture the booted userspace startup and service IPC markers from the NUC11TNKi5.
graduation_criteria: Replace critical launch-path synthetic image tests with fixtures derived from generated userspace image artifacts.
Add stale, truncated, unsigned, and digest-mismatched userspace archive tests to the spec gate.
Keep the QEMU service-startup proof exercising generated-image boot, mailbox, descriptor validation, syscall query, service IPC, fault, and restart paths before native-ready.
next_actions: Create a small generated-image fixture reader for host tests.
Replace the marked model-only launch and service synthetic fixtures with generated userspace image fixtures.
Extend userspace archive generation tests around production_artifact_manifest.zig.
Capture the service-startup marker group in the NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof bundle.

tracks.title: Booted permission review and policy mediation
current_evidence: Freestanding QEMU boots now run the permission review flow before native-ready using generated app packages, the permission review service task, compositor-backed review rendering, policy mediation, and explicit grant/deny markers.

The native smoke marker contract requires review-port readiness, policy-port readiness, rendered review output, zero-authority denials, local grants, explicit device/media decisions, and lease expiry evidence.
The NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof marker file requires the same permission review markers from real hardware serial output.
production_gaps: The booted permission proof is QEMU-backed; the first real hardware proof bundle has not captured the same markers yet.
Interactive physical input for permission review remains represented by the profiled boot review plan until xHCI keyboard input is wired into the review loop on the hardware target.
graduation_criteria: Keep permission review markers release-gated in QEMU before native-ready and require the same markers in the hardware proof bundle.
Replace profiled permission review input with real hardware input events once the NUC11TNKi5 xHCI path is available.
Reject hardware proof bundles that omit review rendering, grant, deny, and lease-expiry markers.
next_actions: Capture permission review markers in build/hardware-proofs/nuc11tnki5/serial.log.
Wire NUC11TNKi5 xHCI keyboard input into the permission review service and retire the profiled hardware path.

tracks.title: Live sync and private overlay transport
current_evidence: Sync state covers device graph enrollment, durable inbound/outbound frame queues, replay rejection, selective policy, per-object sharing, CRDT merge semantics, secret transfer markers, transactional database contracts, and explicit conflict review/resolution.
The overlay relay service rejects unauthorized relay use and target changes in harnessed tests.

End-to-end host tests replicate document, media, secret, and database payloads between two service tasks through a booted relay fallback model, and prove object-scoped grants skip private entries while offline conflicts stay reviewable.

The two-node QEMU gate boots separate native nodes with separate native-store images and now requires booted device graph, policy, device-to-device, relay, revoked-device, and persisted sync-service restart markers on each node.
production_gaps: The booted QEMU proof still observes native sync markers rather than a completed async network driver with packet capture, replay-window, reconnect, and congestion behavior.
Real-hardware evidence still needs to capture the same sync markers on the NUC11TNKi5 with the Intel I225-LM path active.
Device identity depends on the boot/attestation production root track before remote trust can be considered production-grade.
graduation_criteria: Replace sync_transport_harness as the primary evidence with a native transport service that runs through endpoint syscalls and the network driver task.
Keep the two-node QEMU replication gate covering offline policy, device-to-device replication, relay fallback, revoked-device rejection, and persisted restart before release.
Bind remote device sessions to production attestation roots or explicitly mark them local-lab only.
next_actions: Define the transport service ABI and move packet submission out of the harness module.
Promote conflict review and object-scoped sync grants into the rendered shell review surface.
Extend the two-QEMU sync harness with packet-capture assertions once the network driver task owns real frames.

tracks.title: Notes and docs daily-driver slice
current_evidence: The rendered-shell production journey is now scoped to one Notes app daily-driver path rather than a generic desktop expansion path.

The journey installs a signed native Notes package, starts its native component, opens a notes workspace and document, reviews the local object-access permission, grants an object-scoped collaborative share, syncs only after sharing, updates and rolls back the package, recovers shell/runtime state, removes the package, and revokes device and policy authority.
The share step writes a concrete trusted-overlay, object-scoped workspace grant and verifies the collaborator can read and write the shared note before sync proceeds.

Task-flow ledger evidence now includes share_document alongside install_app, open_workspace, open_document, review_permission_request, sync_workspace, update_app, rollback_app_update, recover_system, and remove_app.
production_gaps: The slice proof is still a host/service journey; the same ordered path is not yet a booted QEMU marker group or real-hardware capture.
The Notes editor behavior is represented by document open, permission review, share, and sync service state rather than text input/editing through a booted UI loop.
Native package install/update proof uses signed manifest state and package-service lifecycle rather than loading a realistic Notes app asset bundle through a public store channel.
graduation_criteria: Keep the first daily-driver scenario narrow: Notes app install, notes workspace/document use, explicit permission review, object-scoped sharing, local-first sync, update rollback, recovery, and package removal.
Promote the ordered host journey into QEMU native smoke markers before broadening desktop surface area.
Require the same journey markers in the NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof bundle before calling the slice production-ready.
next_actions: Add booted native smoke markers for the Notes package install/open/share/sync/update/recover path.
Route a minimal text edit through the booted shell input loop and assert the edited note survives sync and recovery.
Capture the complete Notes daily-driver marker group in build/hardware-proofs/nuc11tnki5/serial.log.

tracks.title: Userspace driver data-plane depth
current_evidence: Driver registration checks signed bundles, device-class authority, DMA range metadata, restart generations, and a constrained first target of brokered programmed-I/O ATA with programmed DMA domains rather than bus-master DMA.
Storage driver tasks attach through the kernel device broker and the ATA bootstrap path exports checked read/write bridges for freestanding volume access.

The driver boundary spec gate exercises brokered ATA read/write I/O, programs an IOMMU-style DMA domain, authorizes brokered DMA buffers, and rejects stale task authority, stale DMA buffers, stale broker sessions, expired leases, invalid ports, explicit broker revocation, and post-restart target generation mismatches.

The storage data-plane gate covers timeout propagation, active-I/O restart, and partial-transfer recovery by proving incomplete ATA writes are discarded before a restarted userspace driver reissues I/O.

The native network driver path reauthorizes brokered service-identity sends through the egress broker, so revoked network-policy capabilities stop already-open userspace network paths before transmit.

QEMU driver restart proof performs broker-mediated storage reads and writes before and after restart, rejects stale authority, stale DMA buffer, and stale port access after generation change, gates the new broker session rebind, and is now required by the real-hardware proof marker contract.
production_gaps: Only the bootstrap storage path has concrete hardware-like data-plane depth; other driver classes remain inventory, policy, or publication proofs.
IOMMU and DMA isolation now have executable native programming and brokered-buffer evidence, but not real VT-d/AMD-Vi page-table programming or device fault capture.
The timeout, partial-transfer, and explicit revocation cases are host spec gates; QEMU coverage now gates brokered restart and rebind while hardware packet/block I/O evidence is still pending.
graduation_criteria: Add broker-mediated data-plane tests for at least storage and network that run in QEMU and prove no kernel direct publication for excluded subsystems.
Replace the native IOMMU model with real hardware programming and fault evidence before broadening the first production target beyond brokered programmed-I/O storage.
Gate driver restart on active I/O recovery, broker revocation, rebind, and no stale DMA or port access after generation change.
next_actions: Move timeout, partial transfer, and explicit broker revocation proofs into the focused QEMU driver restart gate.
Bind the native DMA-domain model to real VT-d/AMD-Vi programming and archive device-fault evidence before enabling bus-master DMA targets.
Capture the expanded driver restart/rebind marker group, including DMA-domain and brokered-buffer markers, in the NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof bundle.

tracks.title: Resource scheduler and live platform telemetry
current_evidence: Scheduler decisions account for resource class, engine availability, thermal pressure, battery saver, privacy mode, CPU budget, memory bandwidth, and zero-copy shared memory.
Booted provider tests derive hardware-source telemetry from live runtime counters instead of purely synthetic state.
Telemetry now flows through an explicit provider boundary with test-only host fakes and production freestanding provider descriptors.
Negative tests require observed telemetry before waking hardware queues.
production_gaps: The freestanding provider is still assembled from native runtime counters and test-provided platform fields, not real ACPI, battery, thermal, GPU, NPU, or media driver sources.
There is no scheduler latency, fairness, starvation, or thermal regression gate under sustained load.
Accelerator availability is represented by booleans rather than device queue ownership and completion interrupts.
graduation_criteria: Introduce platform telemetry providers for the first supported target and mark emulator-only providers as test-only.
Add benchmark gates for scheduler latency, fairness across resource classes, background throttling, and thermal/battery policy transitions.
Tie accelerator claims to brokered device queues or explicitly limit production support to CPU/media classes.
next_actions: Replace the freestanding runtime-counter bridge with first-target ACPI, battery, thermal, GPU, NPU, and media driver readers.
Add scheduler benchmark fixtures that run under the existing QEMU benchmark target.
Add regression tests for starvation and privacy-sensitive workload throttling.
